decisions.migration_notes: The assignment policy module (modules/curated/identity-governance/entitlement-management/assignment-policies) adds multiple choice and localized requestor questions and optional access reviews. No caller needs to change anything: a caller that uses neither the new input nor a new question attribute sends a byte-identical request body, so the first plan after the upgrade shows no change of the policy. The questions input keeps text, is_required, is_answer_editable and sequence with their defaults, and its object type gains the optional attributes type ("text_input", the default, or "multiple_choice"), localizations ({ text, language_code }), is_single_line_question and regex_pattern for text questions, and is_multiple_selection_allowed and choices ({ text, actual_value, localizations }) for multiple choice questions. A new attribute that is null is left out of the body; a multiple choice question always sends isMultipleSelectionAllowed, false by default. A value of the earlier object type converts to the new one, so a configuration that passes questions through its own typed variable keeps working. The eight new validations on questions check only the new attributes: the type, at least one choice for a multiple choice question, attributes of one question type rejected on the other, distinct actual_value entries, non-empty choice and localized texts, language codes of two letters with an optional two-letter country, and each language at most once per localizations list. The new optional input review_settings (default null) configures recurring access reviews of the policy's assignments; the module sends reviewSettings only when it is set. Microsoft Learn does not say what an update without reviewSettings does to reviews configured in the admin center or by another tool, so to stop reviews set is_enabled = false and apply before removing the input. Access reviews of access package assignments need Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite. Verified with mocked providers only; not verified in a licensed tenant.
decisions.summary: Assignment policies accept multiple choice and localized questions and optional access reviews, without changing the request body of existing callers

decisions.migration_notes: 30 object inputs of 26 modules, 7 in v1.0 and 23 in beta, gain optional attributes that Microsoft Graph added to the types they contain: cloudLicensing on user and device objects in beta, recapUrl on beta online meeting AI insights, and vapidPublicKey, webPushEncryptionP256dhPublicKey and webPushEncryptionSecret on subscription objects in v1.0, among others listed in interface-changes.json. No attribute is removed or changes its type. Existing values convert to the new types unchanged, the new attributes default to null, and null attributes are left out of requests, so no change is needed.
decisions.summary: Add the optional attributes that Microsoft Graph added to nested object types

decisions.migration_notes: The curated catalog grows from 13 to 17 modules, more than the release gate's 10 percent inventory shift threshold. Every change is an addition: modules/curated/directory/administrative-units, modules/curated/groups/members, modules/curated/identity-governance/entitlement-management/connected-organizations and modules/curated/naming are new, and no curated module is removed or moved. Existing configurations need no change; each new module's README describes its inputs, permissions and lifecycle.
decisions.summary: Add four curated modules: administrative units, group members, connected organizations and naming

decisions.migration_notes: The current Microsoft Graph metadata documents these properties as read-only, or no longer defines them, so the service does not accept them in create or update requests. (1) Removed inputs (variable_removed, 7 v1.0 and 4 beta): permission of the 7 v1.0 access review decisions modules under identity-and-access/identity-governance (access-reviews/unified/decisions, access-reviews/unified/instances/by-access-review-instance-id/decisions and the five by-path-*/decisions modules); nist_classifications of beta reports/directory/recommendations; and capabilities of the beta cloud-pc-pools modules under device-and-app-management (device-management/virtual-endpoint, me and users/by-user-id), because the beta cloudPcPool type no longer has a capabilities property. Delete these arguments from your module blocks; a module block that still sets one fails at plan time with an unsupported argument error. (2) additional_properties now rejects these keys (validation_changed, 7 v1.0 and 1 beta): permission in the same 7 v1.0 decisions modules and nistClassifications in beta reports/directory/recommendations. Remove the key from additional_properties; leaving it fails the input validation at plan time. (3) Nested attributes removed from object inputs (variable_type_changed, 14 v1.0 and 3 beta): permission from the access review decision objects in 11 decisions, stages and instances inputs of 8 v1.0 access review modules, and groupDisplayName from the delegated administration role assignments in the delegated_administration_role_assignments and policy_snapshot inputs of the tenant-governance modules in v1.0 and beta (3 inputs each). Terraform drops an object attribute that the type no longer declares, so existing values still plan, and the attribute is no longer sent; no change is needed, but you can delete the attribute from your values. interface-changes.json lists every accepted key.
decisions.summary: Stop accepting Microsoft Graph properties that the current metadata documents as read-only or no longer defines

decisions.migration_notes: generated/v1.0/change-notifications/subscriptions gains the optional inputs vapid_public_key, web_push_encryption_p256dh_public_key and web_push_encryption_secret, which Microsoft Graph added to subscriptions in v1.0. vapidPublicKey and webPushEncryptionSecret join the inputs whose change replaces the subscription, because Microsoft Graph updates only expirationDateTime and notificationUrl in place (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/subscription-update). The first plan after upgrading replaces every existing subscription managed by this module once, even when the new inputs stay unset: the record of replacing inputs gains the two keys, which Terraform plans as an in-place update of terraform_data.immutable, and replace_triggered_by then replaces msgraph_resource.this. The old subscription is deleted before the new one is created, so notifications stop until the new subscription exists, and the new subscription has a new id that anything which stored the old id must read again. Checked with terraform plan against a state written by the previous release's record. Upgrade when a short notification gap is acceptable, for example together with a planned renewal.
decisions.summary: Replace v1.0 change-notification subscriptions when the new web push inputs change
